title: Hyperdeterminant wavefunctions
authors: Guan-Lin Lin, Di Xiao, Ying Ran
abstract: We systematically introduce hyperdeterminant wavefunctions as a variational-wavefunction-based theoretical framework for strongly correlated quantum states of matter, together with practical numerical simulation algorithms. This framework generalizes previously known fermionic parton constructions, yields reliable microscopics with intuitive physical pictures, and allows direct access to the fractionalized degrees of freedom together with associated microscopic effective field theories. We demonstrate the applications of this framework to fractional Chern insulators and quantum spin liquids. We comment that the hyperdeterminant states belong to a more general class of variational wavefunctions: the fused Gaussian states.
summary: This paper introduces Hyperdeterminant wavefunctions as a powerful, generalized variational method for studying strongly correlated quantum matter. It allows researchers to access fractionalized degrees of freedom crucial for understanding topological phases like FCI and QSLs. The framework provides both theoretical tools (VMPI) and numerical algorithms (PE) to derive effective field theories for these complex systems.
main_problem: Developing a theoretical framework to microscopically investigate strongly correlated quantum states of matter, particularly those exhibiting fractionalized degrees of freedom.
main_result: The authors introduce Hyperdeterminant (Hdet) wavefunctions as a general variational approach that provides access to fractionalized degrees of freedom and yields reliable microscopic effective field theories for systems like FCI and QSLs.
method: The framework utilizes Hdet wavefunctions, which are generalized from Slater determinants, combined with Variational Manifold Path Integral (VMPI) techniques and Projective Expansion (PE) algorithms for numerical simulation.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to strongly correlated quantum states of matter, specifically modeling Fractional Chern Insulators (FCI) and Quantum Spin Liquids (QSL). The formalism generalizes fermionic parton constructions beyond standard electron degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Microscopic effective field theories, Ward identities for gauge fluctuations, and the structure of the fusion tensor defining the Hdet state.
important_parameters: The rank ($r$) of the underlying tensors, which dictates bosonic or fermionic statistics; lattice parameters governing correlation strength.
main_assumptions: Simulating generic Hdet wavefunctions is NP-hard, necessitating approximations like PE. The framework assumes a locality structure for physical reasonableness.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mathematical construction of Hdet states by comparing submatrix selection in Slater determinants versus tensor contraction using the fusion tensor.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces Hdet wavefunctions, establishes their locality structure, demonstrates applications to QSL and FCI models, derives effective theories via VMPI, and concludes with numerical simulation techniques (PE).
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state correlations, the development of a general variational framework applicable to fractionalized excitations is mathematically rich and could inspire new ways to model complex quantum dynamics in AMO systems.
